blocks.content: Quiz: In SpeedBlip's responsive design plan, what renders on screens smaller than 768px instead of the sidebar?
Tap an option below to answer:
A hamburger menu that opens a full-screen overlay navigation
SpeedBlip does not use a hamburger menu. A hamburger requires an extra tap to access navigation - the bottom nav provides always-visible navigation with no extra interaction.
SpeedBlip does not use a hamburger menu. A hamburger requires an extra tap to access navigation - the bottom nav provides always-visible navigation with no extra interaction.
A collapsible top navigation bar with icon-only labels
The top navigation bar is for the landing page (LandingNavbar). The app layout uses a different navigation pattern for small screens.
The top navigation bar is for the landing page (LandingNavbar). The app layout uses a different navigation pattern for small screens.
A bottom navigation bar with icon and label pairs
Correct. SpeedBlip's BottomNav component renders at the bottom of the viewport on mobile screens, giving users always-visible access to all four app sections without any tap to open.
Correct. SpeedBlip's BottomNav component renders at the bottom of the viewport on mobile screens, giving users always-visible access to all four app sections without any tap to open.
No navigation - users swipe between pages
Swipe-based navigation would require gesture handling and provide no visible affordance for where users can go. SpeedBlip uses explicit navigation on all screen sizes.
Swipe-based navigation would require gesture handling and provide no visible affordance for where users can go. SpeedBlip uses explicit navigation on all screen sizes.
